facts.statement: Calendar Spread (Time Spread): Strategy pairing options of the same strike price K but different expiration dates. Sells short-dated option to harvest accelerated Theta decay while buying longer-dated option.

Long Straddle: Simultaneously buying a call and a put with the same strike K and expiration date T. Initial Cost = c + p. Payoff = max(S_T - K, K - S_T) = |S_T - K|. Maximum Loss = c + p (at S_T = K). Upper Breakeven = K + (c + p); Lower Breakeven = K - (c + p).
Hull Section 12.4 Straddle Example: S0 = $69, K = $70, c = $4.00, p = $3.00. Total Cost = $7.00. Max loss = $7.00. Upper Breakeven = $70 + $7 = $77.00. Lower Breakeven = $70 - $7 = $63.00.

Strips and Straps (Asymmetric Straddles): A Strip combines 1 Call + 2 Puts (bearish volatility bias). A Strap combines 2 Calls + 1 Put (bullish volatility bias), both sharing the same strike K and expiration T.

Long Strangle: Buying an out-of-the-money put with strike K1 and an out-of-the-money call with strike K2 (K1 < K2) with same expiration T. Costs strictly less than a straddle (c2 + p1 < c + p), but requires a larger price move to reach profitability. Upper Breakeven = K2 + (c2 + p1); Lower Breakeven = K1 - (c2 + p1).

Hull Section 12.4 Strangle Example: S0 = $54, Put strike K1 = $50 (p = $1.50), Call strike K2 = $60 (c = $2.00). Total Cost = $3.50. Max Loss = $3.50 (if $50 <= S_T <= $60). Upper Breakeven = $60 + $3.50 = $63.50. Lower Breakeven = $50 - $3.50 = $46.50.

Business Snapshot 12.2: Earnings Announcements & Implied Volatility Crush: Prior to major earnings releases, implied volatility spikes sharply as uncertainty mounts. Immediately post-announcement, volatility collapses ('IV Crush'), causing long straddles and strangles to lose value even if the stock makes a significant move.

Master Strategy Matrix: Straddles maximize gamma and vega for explosive event moves; Strangles reduce dollar cost at the expense of a wider breakeven corridor; Calendar spreads monetize theta decay under range-bound consolidation.
